claims.text: Coherent nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby enhance alloy strength.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Dislocation transmission across coherent interfaces relieves stress concentrations that could cause premature crack initiation.
Stress relief and strain redistribution by coherent interfaces preserve ductility under dynamic loading.
Controlled processing can generate finely dispersed coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten refractory HEA.
An eutectic AlCoCrFeNi alloy can serve as the proposed single-phase matrix containing coherent nanoprecipitates.
Processing can be varied to promote or suppress nanoprecipitate formation or coherence while otherwise retaining a comparable HEA.
The coherent nanoprecipitate phase remains stable during testing at room and moderately elevated temperatures.
Dynamic recovery or recrystallization may occur under the proposed testing conditions.
Relative to an alloy lacking coherent nanoprecipitates, the precipitate-containing HEA will have increased yield strength.
The increased strength produced by coherent nanoprecipitates will coexist with high tensile ductility.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will improve strain-rate sensitivity relative to the baseline.
TEM will show dislocations being impeded by nanoprecipitates and efficiently transmitted across precipitate–matrix interfaces.
The mechanism operates only over an optimal moderate range of nanoprecipitate volume fraction, size, and coherence.
The mechanism may fail when precipitates are coarse or incoherent.
The mechanism may fail when alloy composition causes uncontrolled multiphase segregation.
The quantitative contribution of coherent nanoprecipitates to dynamic strength and ductility is not yet established and may vary among alloy systems and processing routes.
Comparable strength, ductility, strain-rate response, and dislocation behavior in matched variants with and without coherent nanoprecipitates would falsify the proposed mechanism.
